title: ChatGPT for SNES
lede: An unofficial Super Nintendo cartridge runs a tiny chat model of about 2.2 million parameters on the Super FX 2 chip, built by Benj Edwards with AI coding agents.

points: Its training conversations were written by OpenAI's open-weight gpt-oss-120b; OpenAI did not make or endorse it.
The model knows about 8,000 words and is openly described as wrong often, not a useful assistant.
An optional build adds a fact book of 150,000 Simple English Wikipedia openings on an MSU-1 data file that the model can look up.
Version 0.7 runs in a browser Snes9x emulator, or on hardware through a flash cart with Super FX support.

points.text: One commenter marvels that transformers could have run on 1990 consumer hardware; a reply says running a model is not the same as creating it.
A skeptic says a model this small is little more than a Markov chain producing English-shaped nonsense.
Much of the thread is people sharing the absurd answers they got, delivered with affection.
Commenters like the presentation, especially the on-screen keyboard typing and its sound effects.
